items.textToSpeech: For everyone aged 1+, the Adequate Intake for Vitamin D is 15 micrograms per day, under conditions of assumed minimal cutaneous vitamin D synthesis. For those aged 7-11 months, the Adequate Intake for vitamin D is 10 micrograms per day. In the presence of endogenous cutaneous vitamin D synthesis, the requirement for dietary vitamin D is lower or may even be zero.

The Adequate Intake is the average observed or experimentally determined approximations or estimates of nutrient intake that is assumed to be adequate. For the European Union, Dietary Reference Values are published by the European Food Safety Authority Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies. Is there anything else I can help you with?
